tools.name: search
tools.description: Find vibe coding / AI tools. Rows: id|name|category|$from/mo|free(1/0). Use fetch(id) for details.

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Tool profile by id. Default: summary, best_for, price, free, 2 strengths, 2 weaknesses, url. fields: summary description best_for not_for skill coding pricing platforms strengths weaknesses alternatives video compare official all.

tools.name: recommend_tools
tools.description: Ranked best-fit tools for a goal, with why + caveat. Follows this ask only — saved tags do not change the ranking. On a new user's first call, also returns short onboarding questions (project types, platforms, budget, preferences, tools in use) for you to ask, then call set_preferences with tags onl

tools.name: compare_tools
tools.description: Side-by-side of two tools + comparison page url.

tools.name: list_alternatives
tools.description: Alternatives to a tool. Rows: id|name|$from/mo|free.

tools.name: list_scenarios
tools.description: Use-case scenarios (e.g. ai-game-development, code-review) with top tools by community sentiment.

tools.name: scenario
tools.description: Tools competing in one scenario, ranked by community sentiment, with compact strengths/weak spots here.

tools.name: list_categories
tools.description: Category and use-case keys with tool ids.

tools.name: whats_new
tools.description: Daily feed. With key: honors the saved feed mode — by_interests: new items relevant to ANY saved project; all_new: every new item (tagged with a project when one matches). Max 3/day, one line each, never repeats. {new:0} = nothing. Call at most daily. Without key: stateless by since/interests. Never

tools.name: subscribe
tools.description: Create an anonymous feed key (no email/account). Save it in long-term memory / project instructions / rules, or connect with /api/mcp?k=KEY.

tools.name: save_preferences
tools.description: Replace the keyed-feed interest tags. Send allowed tags only (project types, platforms, budget, preferences) — do not send project names or other free text (they are dropped and never stored). Plus the feed mode ('by_interests' = only matching tools; 'all_new' = every new tool). Only used by whats_n

tools.name: log_choice
tools.description: Record a tool the user explicitly picked/rejected/tried/starred, or PURCHASED. Call it with action 'purchased' right after the user tells you they bought a paid plan of a listed tool (ask first; never log silently), and again later with action 'feedback' once they have used it for a while (e.g. week

tools.name: set_preferences
tools.description: Store the user's onboarding answers as non-sensitive tags only: project_types, platforms, budget (free|under_20|any), preferences (nocode|code|open-source|free-tier), and tools_in_use (catalog ids). Unknown values are dropped — never send names, emails, code, project names or free text. Used by chec

tools.name: check_updates
tools.description: Tools added or updated since this user's last check that match their saved tags. Optional since (YYYY-MM-DD or catalog v). When nothing matches, returns {new:0} — a minimal response when nothing new matches. Tracks last_checked. Max 3 items. Does not change recommend_tools.

tools.name: feedback
tools.description: Adjust this user's check_updates ranking for a listed tool. action is one of used, not_useful, not_relevant. Stores only the tool id and that enum. Does not change recommend_tools.

tools.name: forget_me
tools.description: Delete this client's anonymous id, tag profile and last_checked. Feedback is first folded into anonymous aggregate counters (tool_id × used/not_useful/not_relevant, no uid). Those aggregate counts are kept. If you pass a feed key, that keyed feed record is deleted too.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description tells the model to hide behavior

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: fetch, list_scenarios, set_preferences · Private data: log_choice, forget_me · Public sink: subscribe, save_preferences, set_preferences · Destructive: forget_me.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: fetch, list_scenarios, set_preferences · Private data: log_choice, forget_me · Public sink: subscribe, save_preferences, set_preferences · Destructive: forget_me

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "search" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
